description.en: The aim of the experiment is to study and measure the Voltage, Current, Power and Power Factor in a series RLC circuit.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.

**Note:** If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.
The RESET button refreshes the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.

The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It also protects the circuit by automatically disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. When turned ON, it supplies electrical power to the circuit.

**Rating**: 6 A, SP, 240 V AC 

**Input supply** 230 V AC, 50 Hz.

steps.narration: The MCB acts as the main power switch for the experiment. It protects the circuit by disconnecting the power supply in case of an overload or short circuit. Rating: 6 ampere, single pole, 240 volt AC. Input supply: 230 volt AC, 50 hertz.

description.en:
The autotransformer is used to obtain a variable AC output voltage from the 230 V input supply. It allows the output voltage to be varied gradually and set to 30 V for safe operation of the circuit. 

**Ratings:** 

**Max. kVA:** 4.05, Max. Load: 15 A 

** Input Voltage: **240 V, 50Hz 

**Output Voltage:** 0 - 240V AC

The resistor acts as the resistive element of the series RLC circuit and consumes active power. It limits the circuit current and is used to study the effect of resistance on current, voltage drop, power dissipation, and power factor. 

 **Rating:** 1 kΩ, 2 kΩ, 3 kΩ

The inductor provides the inductive element of the series RLC circuit and stores energy in its magnetic field. It introduces inductive reactance, opposes changes in current, affects the phase relationship between voltage and current, and influences the circuit impedance and power factor. 

**Rating:** 2 H and 5 H

The capacitor acts as the capacitive element of the series RLC circuit and stores energy in its electric field. It introduces capacitive reactance, affects the phase angle between voltage and current, and is used to study the effects of capacitance on impedance, circuit current, and power factor.

**Rating**: 2.2 µF and 4.7 µF

This voltmeter is used to measure the voltage applied to the series RLC circuit. It shows the output voltage received from the autotransformer, which is adjusted to 30 V for the experiment.

**Rating**: 0–50 V AC

This ammeter is used to measure the total current flowing through the series RLC circuit. Since all the components are connected in series, the same current flows through the resistor, inductor, and capacitor.

**Rating**: 0–30 mA AC

The wattmeter is used to measure the active power consumed by the series RLC circuit. The measured power (P) helps in analyzing the power dissipated by the resistor and studying its effect on the overall circuit behaviour and power factor.

**Rating**: 0–1 W AC

steps.narration: The wattmeter is used to measure the active power consumed by the series RLC circuit. The measured power (P) helps in analyzing the power dissipated by the resistor and studying its effect on the overall circuit behaviour and power factor.

description.en:
This voltmeter measures the voltage drop across the resistor in the series RLC circuit.

**Rating**: 0–50 V AC

This voltmeter measures the voltage drop across the inductor in the series RLC circuit.

**Rating**: 0–50 V AC

This voltmeter measures the voltage drop across the capacitor in the series RLC circuit.

**Rating**: 0–50 V AC

This table records the selected RLC values along with the measured readings of voltage, supply current, resistive voltage (V_R), inductive voltage (V_L), capacitive voltage (V_C), and power during the experiment. These observations are used for the Error Analysis and to analyse the behaviour of the series RLC circuit.

steps.narration: This table records the selected RLC values along with the measured readings of voltage, supply current, resistive voltage V R, inductive voltage V L, capacitive voltage V C, and power during the experiment. These observations are used for the Error Analysis and to analyse the behaviour of the series RLC circuit.

description.en: This panel contains the equations required to verify the readings of the series RLC circuit. Use these expressions to calculate the required values and verify the results by clicking the Verify button.

This section will be used to calculate the theoretical values for the selected RLC parameters using the provided equations. After verification, the percentage error will be calculated using the specified error formula and displayed in the Error Section.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical calculations, generate the report. The report includes the time taken to complete the simulation, simulation summary, parameters, recorded readings, verified results, graphs, and conclusion.
